leading_positions.synthesis: Both prefer targeted protein degradation with the same three names (Crews, Deshaies, Handa) and a citation built on recruiting E3 ligases. Both list B050 as an alternative, and Somfai, Zou and Aili name B042 as an alternative. Both also flag that PROTACs and molecular glues may be two lineages, that Ciulli, Gray, Sakamoto, Kim and Ito are excluded by a three-name cut, and that no PROTAC drug is yet approved. They differ on emphasis: Aqvist stresses the simple chemical idea and clinical programmes, while Brzezinski wants the expert reports to state what remains unsettled before a citation spanning both strands is fixed.

Both prefer programmable base editing without double-strand cleavage as a defined chemical reaction. They differ on attribution: Chabes proposes Liu, Komor and Gaudelli, while Linke proposes Liu alone as one part of a two-part prize. Both flag overlap with the 2020 CRISPR-Cas9 prize, the youth of the field, and the unresolved place of Nishida and Kondo (Target-AID). Chabes says his preference would yield to a more clearly chemical modality such as B042 if base editing is judged medicine or biotechnology.

Both prefer ionizable lipid nanoparticles for nucleic-acid delivery, citing pKa-tuned charge switching, lipid phase behaviour and clinical proof at scale. They differ on names: Aili proposes Cullis, Hope and Anderson, while Linke proposes Cullis and Hope only. Both note the Vancouver and Boston lineages overlap and that the 2023 Medicine prize on nucleoside-modified mRNA covers adjacent territory.

Only the chair prefers a two-part prize combining base editing and lipid nanoparticles. No other member's round-1 configuration includes both ballots. Aili and Chabes each list the other topic or B042 as alternatives, but alternatives are not preferred configurations and are not counted here.

Sparr alone prefers biomolecular phase separation (Hyman, Brangwynne, Rosen), as a physical-chemical concept distinct from a method or modality. She concedes the in vivo generality is debated, that part of the evidence is cell-biological, and that she may overvalue it as a soft-matter specialist. Aili also doubts its maturity.

Somfai alone prefers palladium-catalysed C-N coupling (Buchwald, Hartwig) as a settled, two-person, molecule-making achievement. He concedes that the 2010 C-C coupling prize may make it look redundant, that opening support was narrow, and that Kosugi precedence is unverified.

Zou alone prefers rational design of molecular-sieve catalysts (Corma, Davis, Zones), with decades of industrial validation and checkable structural evidence. He concedes diffuse credit (Yu, Tsapatsis and others excluded), a weaker novelty narrative for a lay audience, and his own field proximity.

areas_of_agreement: No candidate has majority support: the eight round-1 files name six different lead ballots (B042, B050, B052, B024, B029, B003), and the largest explicit groups are two members each for B042, B050 and B052.
B042 and B050 are the alternatives named most often: B042 appears in the alternatives of Aili, Chabes, Linke, Somfai and Zou, and B050 in those of Aili, Aqvist, Brzezinski and Somfai.

Several members who prefer different ballots (Aili, Aqvist, Brzezinski, Linke, Somfai, Zou) list B042 as a preferred configuration or alternative, so it is the most widely acceptable second choice across the files.
Every member states that a three-laureate cap leaves out credible contributors, and nearly every member names attribution as the main reservation about their own first choice.
Members state their reservations about their own preferred candidate openly, including Sparr and Zou on field proximity and Somfai on unverified precedence.
scientific_disputes: Whether base editing (B050) is chemistry or medicine and biotechnology: Chabes, Aqvist, Brzezinski, Zou and Linke all raise this, in some form, as open.
Whether delivery chemistry (B052) is a distinct chemical invention, as Aili and Linke argue, or the vehicle for a payload already honoured by the 2023 Medicine prize.
Whether targeted protein degradation (B042) is one coherent chemical idea or two (PROTACs and glues), and whether the clinical record is enough without an approved PROTAC drug.
Whether biomolecular phase separation (B024) is a general organising principle or a still-disputed one, with some reported droplets possibly artefacts.
Whether palladium C-N coupling (B029) adds a new chemical principle beyond the 2010 prize, and whether rational zeolite design (B003) is conceptually new or a refinement of a mature technology.
attribution_disputes: B042: Crews, Deshaies and Handa (Aqvist, Brzezinski) leave out Ciulli, Gray, Sakamoto, Kim and Ito. Whether Handa or Ciulli takes the third seat depends on whether the glue strand is part of the prize.
B050: Chabes names Liu, Komor and Gaudelli, Linke names Liu alone, and Aili names the three-person version. Nishida and Kondo (Target-AID) are not in any configuration.
B052: Aili proposes Cullis, Hope and Anderson, Linke proposes Cullis and Hope. Madden, MacLachlan and Langer are left out and the Vancouver and Boston lineages overlap.
B024: Sparr names Hyman, Brangwynne and Rosen, noting that Pappu and Mittag are credible additions. B003: Zou names Corma, Davis and Zones while Yu and Tsapatsis are excluded.
B029: Somfai names Buchwald and Hartwig and has not verified the precedence of Kosugi's earlier tin-amide work.
maturity_disputes: B050 dates from 2016 and 2017, so durable clinical safety, off-target deamination and bystander edits are not yet established (Chabes). Aili and Linke both note the proximity to the 2020 CRISPR prize.
B042 has mature mechanism and many clinical programmes but few approved drugs, which Aqvist, Brzezinski and Aili treat as promissory.
B052 has approved products used at global scale since 2018 (patisiran and mRNA vaccines), which Aili and Linke cite as the maturity advantage over B042 and B050.
B024 is still contested on generality and in vivo function (Sparr, Aili), while B029 and B003 are mature, with settled mechanism or decades of industrial use (Somfai, Zou).
conflict_or_recusal_flags: Sparr discloses scientific adjacency to B052 and B024 through her lipid self-assembly and membrane work, and notes shared Lund affiliation with Linke and Somfai; she reports no personal or institutional tie to a candidate.
Zou discloses that his electron-diffraction work on zeolites places him in the same community as the B003 candidates, with no documented collaboration.

Brzezinski discloses that his respiratory electron and proton transfer research is close to B020 (Gray and Winkler), which he did not make his preferred configuration; he also notes Stockholm University colleagueship with Zou, not relevant to a shortlisted ballot.
Aili discloses a research-field overlap with Sparr in self-assembly and peptide-lipid systems and a translational interest in nanomedicine, with no tie to a nominee that would require recusal.

Chabes notes that his nucleotide metabolism and replication fidelity work is adjacent to B050 without collaboration, and the chair (Linke) reports no connection of Lund or his research group to any shortlisted candidate; Aqvist and Somfai report no specific conflicts.
questions_for_round2: Should the committee decide first whether base editing (B050), now only about a decade old, is a chemistry prize given the 2020 CRISPR-Cas9 prize, and if so should the citation name Liu alone, Liu with Komor and Gaudelli, or include Nishida and Kondo?

For B042, is the prize about the PROTAC concept (Crews, Deshaies), the glue and cereblon strand (Handa), or both, and who takes the third seat (Handa, Ciulli or another) if the citation must cover both strands?
Does the absence of an approved PROTAC drug, set against approved lipid-nanoparticle medicines, change how the committee weighs B042 against B052 on demonstrated consequence?

For B052, how should credit between the Vancouver lineage (Cullis, Hope, Madden, MacLachlan) and the Boston lineage (Anderson, Langer) be divided, and can the citation be written as chemistry (pKa design and lipid phase behaviour) so it does not read as a second recognition of the 2023 mRNA work?

Is a two-part prize in which both parts concern nucleic-acid medicine (B050 plus B052) acceptable, or would a pairing with B042 or a non-medical topic better reflect the range of the field, and which members can accept each pairing?
Can members who prefer B024, B029 or B003 say which of B042, B050 and B052 they would accept, so the committee can see whether any configuration reaches five votes?

Should the expert reports be asked to state what is unsettled in B042 (ternary-complex mechanism, lack of approved PROTAC) and B024 (in vivo generality) before the committee settles on citation wording?
summary.chair_observation: The first round shows a split committee with no candidate near the five votes needed: two members each prefer B042, B050 and B052, and one each prefer B024, B029 and B003. The three nucleic-acid-adjacent or modality topics (B042, B050, B052) recur across preferred configurations and alternatives, while the disagreement is about chemistry versus medicine framing, overlap with earlier prizes, clinical maturity, and how to cut credit to three names. The chair is one of the two supporters of B050 and of B052 and is the only member preferring the two-part pairing, so this summary counts only what is stated explicitly in the eight files.
